core_obligations: Set up the projections from A^r_k times X and the universal divisor H_univ, and let Sigma be the locus where q : H_univ -> A^r_k is not smooth (proof lines 10966-10982).

Note that Sigma is closed because the smooth locus of a morphism is open, and that it suffices to show that q(Sigma) is contained in a proper closed subset of A^r_k, since fibres of a smooth morphism are smooth (proof lines 10982-10985).
Reduce to a dimension bound: Sigma with its reduced structure is of finite type over k, so it is enough to prove dim(Sigma) < r (proof lines 10986-10987).
Establish that dimension bound, which occupies the rest of the proof and uses the hypotheses on X, the generating system and the immersion (remaining lines up to 11057).
proof_roadmap: Build the universal family and its singular locus.
Reduce smoothness of the general member to a properness statement for the image of the singular locus.
Bound the dimension of the singular locus by r - 1.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the Bertini smoothness theorem in the form used by the Stacks Project: for a smooth X over k, a generating system of sections of an invertible sheaf L whose associated morphism to P(V) is an immersion, the general member H_v of the resulting family of divisors is smooth over k'. The proof sets up the universal divisor H_univ inside A^r_k times X, considers the singular locus Sigma of the projection q : H_univ -> A^r_k, argues that Sigma is closed because the smooth locus of a morphism is open, and reduces to proving that the image q(Sigma) is contained in a proper closed subset of A^r_k; since Sigma is of finite type over k it suffices to bound its dimension by r - 1 (proof lines 10966-10987 and the remainder of the proof to line 11057). H3: the dimension count for the singular locus of the universal family is a genuine research-level argument and is the heart of the theorem.
